name: SG Finserve Ltd
title: SG Finserve Ltd - 539199 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SG Finserve FY26 PAT rose 58% to INR 128 crore on a INR 3,936 crore loan book (up 75%), with management guiding AUM growth of 25-30% medium term and 35-40% for FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 operating income of INR 334 crore (up 96% YoY), closing loan book of INR 3,936 crore (up 75%, stated as an all-time high) and PAT of INR 128 crore (up 58%). Q4 PAT was INR 42 crore, up 30% QoQ, and Q4 fee income was about INR 6.2 crore against about INR 1.5-1.9 crore in earlier periods. Management reiterated nil NPA as its guidance and said it is comfortable with leverage of about 1.9x, aiming for 3x over two to three years without fresh equity. Q&A covered NPA philosophy, TReDS entry, related-party exposure and the sharp rise in fee income, and several answers were framed as conservative guidance.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / anchor financing)
segments.commentary: More than three-fourths of the business per management. Construction is the largest sector at about 35% of AUM, followed by automotive; average ticket about INR 5 crore per borrower.

segments.name: Factoring
segments.commentary: Bilateral factoring commercialised in March 2026 with INR 175 crore outstanding at 31 March. TReDS participation expected to go live in Q1 FY27 through RXIL and M1xchange.

segments.name: Cross-sell (LAP, working capital, business loans)
segments.commentary: Opportunistic cross-sell within the anchor/dealer ecosystem at near-zero acquisition cost; management said it is not a core focus. Mobile is about 2% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 25-30% CAGR medium to long term; FY27 aspiration of 35-40% AUM growth.
Profit guidance of 30-35% CAGR, measured on full-year PAT of the previous financial year, not Q4 exit run rate.
Profitability range: ROA 4.5-5%, ROE 14-16%, cost to income 13-17%.
Leverage to rise from about 2x to 3x over two to three years, in phases; comfortable range 2x-3x.
Internal AUM target of INR 10,000 crore in three to four years without fresh equity, with bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore.
NPA guidance remains nil; management said the aim is no losses, while acknowledging that lending involves losses.
capex_capacity: Operates from 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering about a 100 km radius; business is 100% domestic with no import-export financing.
Bank lines of more than INR 3,000 crore, with INR 3,000-3,500 crore estimated, not fully utilised.
Gross disbursements for FY26 crossed INR 25,000 crore; Q4 disbursements about INR 7,700 crore against a book of about INR 3,900 crore (average churn about 45 days).
New businesses (unspecified) are under groundwork, subject to regulatory approvals; timing of FY27 or FY28 uncertain.
demand_pricing: Management said fewer than 100 of the top 500 corporates are active in supply chain finance, and only 25-30% of anchors' sales are covered by organised programmes, so headroom is large.

Management estimated the wider supply chain market, including PSU banks, at upward of INR 1 lakh crore; five to six private banks and a few NBFCs each run AUM of INR 10,000-15,000 crore in dealer finance.
Fee income is being pursued as a strategy; fees on disbursements range from 10 paise to 50 paise, with some cases at 1%.
Management said no stress is visible in top sectors but is monitoring geopolitical and fuel/gas supply risks; steel import effects are yet to be assessed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the business model support nil NPAs, and is there a buffer in NPA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is short-term (about 45-day churn), invoice-backed and end-use monitored, with anchors paid directly and early-warning tracking of dealer cycles. It said Ind AS ECL and RBI rules limit conservative provisioning, with about INR 18 crore provision already held; the guidance is nil NPA by design.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leverage target and how will growth be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage is about 1.9x; management sees 3x as acceptable and aims to reach it in two to three years in phases. Bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore are available, so growth to INR 10,000 crore AUM is possible in three to four years without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee income is now a strategic focus and that Q3 fees were under-captured; it expects Q4-level fees (about INR 6 crore) to become the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% growth guidance conservative, and is FY27 guidance different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is deliberately conservative and aims for 35-40% AUM growth in FY27, with 25-30% as the medium-term average. Earlier conservatism was attributed to a management change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the loan book goes to group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Related-party exposure is less than INR 100 crore; channel financing to group companies is around 30% of the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: Did steel prices drive the AUM increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel price rise did not drive the 31 March AUM; growth came from volume and FY26 average AUM doubled to INR 2,640 crore.

risks_watch: Fee income reliance: Q4 fee income of about INR 6.2 crore is far above prior quarters; sustainability is unproven.
Geopolitical and fuel/gas supply disruption could stress steel, auto and construction borrowers (top sectors), though no stress was reported.
Earlier guidance inconsistency across quarters, which an investor raised; conservative framing may need to be tracked against actuals.
Leverage increase from 1.9x to 3x and the timing of TReDS go-live in Q1 FY27 and of new business approvals.
Concentration in the construction sector (about 35% of AUM).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on conservatism in guidance; more hedged on new businesses, timing of TReDS, and geopolitical impact, which management said is still evolving.
key_quotes: Our closing Loan Book of INR 3,936 crores is at all-time high, which is backed by our core business - supply chain finance
But under-committing, over-delivering is something which suits us best.
By design, by target, we are not going to lose money. So that's why our guidance is NIL NPA.
We don't plan to have TReDS platform. We will only participate on existing TReDS regulated entities licensed by RBI.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.5 crore in Q3 and INR 1.89 crore in Q4 FY25 as cited by analyst
INR 21 crore added from warrant conversion in April 2026

growth.why: Management guides FY27 AUM growth of 35-40% (medium-term 25-30% CAGR), backed by 30 hubs, bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore and TReDS go-live in Q1 FY27, but no specific new capacity is quantified and new businesses remain unspecified.
